requests.discriminates: Complete ordered asset names, sizes and bytes. Go observes these through WalkDir/ReadFile; Rust enumerates the embedded asset table. This is content evidence, not Rust WalkDir coverage.
requests.subject: BundledIndex

requests.discriminates: Both sides call their production filesystem wrapper on LibPath()+"/"+name. Exact case, no extension completion, trimming or dot-segment normalization; missing and malformed asset names remain missing.
requests.subject: BundledLookup

requests.discriminates: the wrapper's path predicate: an exact, case-sensitive, unnormalized bundled:/// prefix test and nothing more. bundled:/// with an empty remainder is bundled, a fourth slash stays inside the remainder, and a traversal after the prefix is still bundled because the predicate never resolves the path. Shortened schemes, a leading character and an upper-case scheme are not. This is the one bundled operation scope.json records as implemented_untested, awaiting exactly this witness.
requests.subject: BundledPath

requests.discriminates: the root every consumer joins asset names onto. An embedded build answers with the scheme path bundled:///libs, not a directory on disk, and that path is itself bundled. A Rust constant that carried a trailing slash, a different scheme or a filesystem path would break every consumer that concatenates a lib name onto it.
requests.subject: BundledLibPath

requests.discriminates: the wrapper dispatch WrapFS installs, which no other case in this group reaches, and the `errors` column of the group's coverage matrix. Eight bundled:/// paths record DirectoryExists, FileExists, GetAccessibleEntries, Stat and Realpath together, which is where the pinned surface is least uniform: bundled:/// is a directory to Stat and lists libs through GetAccessibleEntries, yet DirectoryExists answers false for it, because that method tests rest == "libs" and the scheme root's remainder is empty. A trailing slash, an upper-case LIBS, a fourth slash and libs/../libs are all unknown to every one of the five, so nothing in the dispatch normalizes a path or folds case. Seven walks then record the walk contract: from bundled:/// the first callback receives bundled:////libs, because walkDir joins rest + "/" + name onto a scheme that already ends in a slash; fs.SkipAll stops the walk and WalkDir still returns nil; fs.SkipDir returned for a file entry skips only that entry, so all 108 still arrive; fs.SkipDir returned for the libs directory entry prunes the recursion and ends the walk after one callback; any other error is returned to the caller verbatim; and an unknown bundled directory walks zero entries without an error. Six rows then record the mutation refusals: WriteFile, AppendFile, Remove and Chtimes each panic on a bundled path with the pinned message, whether the asset exists or not, and whether the path is an asset or the scheme root. The Rust side reports a named gap for all of it: tsr_bundled::BundledFs is the counterpart and is reachable only with a direct tsr_vfs dependency this harness does not declare, tsr_vfs::FileSystem has no walk method, and BundledFs overrides none of the trait's mutators, so it would answer Error::Unsupported for every path rather than panicking on a bundled one.
requests.subject: BundledWrapper

requests.discriminates: access outside the checkout, from the Go side. TestingLibPath locates the libs directory through runtime.Caller(0), so it resolves only where the pinned source tree is present; under -trimpath the same call returns the module-relative github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/bundled/libs and does not panic, so the accessor fails silently. The payload records base names, absoluteness, existence and entry count rather than a machine path, so it distinguishes both worlds without freezing anyone's directory layout. crates/tsr_bundled has no counterpart by construction and reports the gap.
